er_v06_rc_b001_01: The Nutrifruit research is with the newspaper. They say they'll have it checked before publishing it.
er_v06_rc_b001_02: Did you tell them about your mother's situation?
er_v06_rc_b001_03: I did. They agreed to include the threat, but they didn't promise they could get her out.
er_v06_rc_b001_05: Yeah. I left an address where they can find me.
er_v06_rc_b001_06: You don't have to tell me we did the right thing.
er_v06_rc_b001_08: I just wanted someone to know that when I made the decision, I didn't forget her.
er_v06_rc_b002_01: The secret behind Pastel's nutrifruit has leaked! A research paper reveals how ordinary nutrifruit can be made to produce seeds again. The same morning, the former head of the station's largest hydroponics farm, imprisoned for embezzlement, was found dead in her cell. Pastel has declined to comment.
er_v06_rc_b002_03: The morning the paper came out, they killed my mother.
er_v06_rc_b002_05: I went to identify her. It wasn't a rumour.
er_v06_rc_b002_06: They said it was a sudden illness. On the very morning the paper came out.
er_v06_rc_b002_08: Don't tell me she would have wanted this. I can't ask her anymore.
er_v06_rc_b002_09: All right. I won't speak for her.
er_v06_rc_b002_10: I know there were other ways. I know why I didn't choose them.
er_v06_rc_b002_11: But knowing that doesn't make this any easier.
er_v06_rc_b002_12: You don't have to decide anything today.
er_v06_rc_b002_13: I want to stay here for a while. Don't ask me if I want a drink.
er_v06_rc_b003_01: They only returned a few of Mother's things.
er_v06_rc_b003_02: Is there anything you want to keep?
er_v06_rc_b003_03: A list she wrote. All little things about the farm.
er_v06_rc_b003_04: Which light was broken, what tools were missing, which grow tank needed checking again.
er_v06_rc_b003_05: She was always thinking about it.
er_v06_rc_b003_06: Yeah. Not every page was research that could change the whole station.
er_v06_rc_b003_07: Most of the time, she was just busy with these things.
er_v06_rc_b003_09: I will. This isn't for sale.
er_v06_rc_b004_01: Thank you. I'll take the food.
er_v06_rc_b004_02: Life has to go on. I know. Just not that fast.
er_v06_rc_b005_03: They approached me. But in the end, I went to them myself.
er_v06_rc_b005_04: They'll help me make Pastel pay, and they can keep me out of the company's reach. The research can keep spreading too.
er_v06_rc_b005_05: Do you know what they want you to do?
er_v06_rc_b005_06: I asked. I'm not going to agree to anything just because someone promises revenge.
er_v06_rc_b005_08: I won't stay in the same place. I can't come here on a fixed schedule anymore.
er_v06_rc_b005_09: Don't turn every meeting into a message drop.
er_v06_rc_b005_10: I won't use your shop as a contact point. You helped me. That doesn't mean you should carry every risk from now on.
er_v06_rc_b005_11: Sometimes, though, I might still need someone I can have an ordinary conversation with.
er_v06_rc_b005_12: You know where this place is.
er_v06_rc_b006_01: All right, I need a weapon. What do you have?
er_v06_rc_b006_02: Do you know how to use one?
er_v06_rc_b006_03: Someone's teaching me. I'm not going to wave around something I can't use just to frighten people.
er_v06_rc_b006_04: Check the condition first. Don't settle for a broken one.
er_v06_rc_b006_05: This time I'll listen to you.
er_v06_rc_b007_01: The money's enough. Don't waive this one for me.
er_v06_rc_b008_01: Then I'll look elsewhere. I'm not in a hurry to take something more likely to hurt me.
er_v06_rc_b009_01: Before, all I wanted was to go back to how things were.
er_v06_rc_b009_02: Now I can't even say what I want to become.
er_v06_rc_b009_03: Then at least don't take everyone's words as truth.
er_v06_rc_b010_01: I'm looking for Eleanor. But she said not to ask around about where she lives.
er_v06_rc_b010_03: I'm not here to take her back. I know how awful that sounds right now.
er_v06_rc_b010_04: I just want to explain what her mother did for my family before. Back then, I did nothing for her.
er_v06_rc_b010_05: When she's willing to listen, tell her yourself.
er_v06_rc_b010_06: All right. I'll wait until she's willing.
er_v06_rc_b010_07: If she needs something normal that can be bought, I can help find it. I don't need to know where she goes.
er_v06_rc_b011_02: Do you want to see her?
er_v06_rc_b011_03: Later. I don't have the energy to teach everyone how to talk to me right now.
er_v06_rc_b012_01: I know there are things between us we never finished saying.
er_v06_rc_b012_02: You don't have to finish them before you leave.
er_v06_rc_b012_03: I care about you. That didn't disappear because something happened to my mother.
er_v06_rc_b012_04: But I can't promise to come back on time, and I can't ask you to stop your life and wait for me.
er_v06_rc_b012_05: Then don't promise something you can't do.
er_v06_rc_b012_06: ...All right. When I can come back, I will.
er_v06_rc_b013_01: I'll remember this place. Not just the research and the investigator's money.
er_v06_rc_b013_02: And remember the first time you turned your nose up at my cup?
er_v06_rc_b013_03: That cup really did have a chip. I wasn't wrong about that.
er_v06_rc_b014_01: I'm here for food for the road. We're leaving with the revolutionaries soon.
er_v06_rc_b014_03: I want it. Now when I see it, I feel like at least some things weren't for nothing.
er_v06_rc_b015_03: You too. Don't take on every trouble that comes to your door.
er_v06_rc_b015_06: Thank you again. For everything. I hope next time we can talk about something else.
er_v06_rd_b001_02: I already handed it over. They promised to release her.
er_v06_rd_b001_07: I asked you to keep it safe, not to decide what my mother is worth.
er_v06_rd_b001_09: I'll look into it myself. From today on, stay out of my business.
er_v06_rd_b002_01: She's out. I just came to tell you. Stop using 'maybe they'll release her' as an excuse for that deal.
er_v06_rd_b002_02: I'll live my own life. You keep running your shop.
er_v06_rd_b003_01: You sold Mother's research disk to someone else?
er_v06_rd_b003_03: So from beginning to end, you really were just waiting for a valuable piece of goods.
er_v06_rd_b003_04: I understand. I was wrong about you.
er_v06_rd_b004_01: That thing in the newspaper. Did you send it?
er_v06_rd_b004_03: But it shouldn't have been you! What gave you the right to decide, behind my back, what my mother would have to pay?
er_v06_rd_b004_04: You can say you did it for everyone's good. Just don't call it a road we chose together.
er_v06_rd_b005_01: I've thought about it. I'll handle what comes next myself.
er_v06_rd_b005_02: What do you plan to do?
er_v06_rd_b005_03: First, find a way to get my mother back. I'll verify their terms one by one.
er_v06_rd_b005_04: Thank you for everything you did for me. Even if we didn't make it to the end, I won't forget it.
er_v06_ep_b001_01: You still haven't fixed that lamp?
er_v06_ep_b001_03: My chipped cup still holds water too. But you clearly said you had intact ones!
er_v06_ep_b001_05: Naturally. How could I be careless about the first account I ever settled with you?
er_v06_ep_b002_01: My mother made too much, so she told me to bring some over.
er_v06_ep_b002_02: How is it always exactly one extra portion?
er_v06_ep_b002_03: Do you want it or not?
er_v06_ep_b002_05: Then ask one fewer question that's hard for the cook to answer.
er_v06_ep_b003_01: I knew that customer just now. He used to tell me not to associate with people down here.
er_v06_ep_b003_02: He seemed happy enough to buy today.
er_v06_ep_b003_03: I told him: if you want to buy something, follow the rules here. If you want to teach me how to pick a boyfriend, please leave.
er_v06_ep_b003_05: Buying. He isn't always that tactless.
er_v06_ep_b004_01: Don't waive this one today. I got paid.
er_v06_ep_b004_02: You don't have to prove you can afford it every time.
er_v06_ep_b004_03: I know. I just want you to know, you're not the only one who can take care of someone.
er_v06_ep_b004_04: Then charge it at full price.
er_v06_ep_b004_05: Yeah. And after that, sit and talk with me for a while.
er_v06_ep_b005_01: I sorted this batch. The faulty ones are together. Don't say I didn't warn you.
er_v06_ep_b005_02: You're starting to sound like a veteran.
er_v06_ep_b005_03: I always was. Don't bring up my first scavenging trip for the rest of my life.
er_v06_ep_b005_04: Then can I bring up your first food shopping trip?
er_v06_ep_b006_01: Let's not talk about all that today. Got anything new in the shop?
er_v06_ep_b006_03: Goods. Preferably the kind I can find a few flaws in.
er_v06_ep_b006_05: Good. Sounds like an ordinary trip to the shop.
er_v06_end_b001_01: Later, she sometimes came from work, sometimes after running errands with her mother. She still complained your lamp wasn't bright enough, still insisted every account be settled to the last credit.
er_v06_end_b001_02: Only now no one had to guess why she kept coming back to this pawnshop.
er_v06_end_b002_01: Before you left, you told her. She first asked whether everything on your journey was arranged, then went through every way of contacting you one by one.
er_v06_end_b002_02: She didn't say it would all be easy. You simply agreed that every step ahead would be explained to each other.
er_v06_end_b003_01: When Eleanor heard, she started asking everywhere for news of you. She remembered how you had verified every promise one by one, and knew that saying 'it'll be fine' was nowhere near enough.
er_v06_end_b003_02: She has yet to find a way to see you, but writes down every name she is given. The next day, she follows them up.
er_v06_end_b004_01: Later, she still came to this shop. No trade, no question waiting for an answer.
er_v06_end_b004_02: What she remembered about you wasn't only the ending, but also those first small accounts, every one calculated so clearly.
er_v06_end_b005_01: She rebuilt her life bit by bit. Sometimes she brought goods, sometimes she introduced business for acquaintances.
er_v06_end_b005_02: You never became lovers, but she would never again see the lower levels as merely a place she had to endure.
er_v06_end_b006_01: Her messages didn't always reach you. When she appeared, it wasn't always to talk about research or the Revolution.
er_v06_end_b006_02: Sometimes she only asked whether your shop was still open. She remembered that in this pawnshop, she could be just Eleanor.
er_v06_end_b007_01: She never came again. Everything you heard about her came from other customers.
er_v06_end_b007_02: The pawnshop's ledger recorded that income, but no column could record who had been missing from then on.
